Shlōsh Esréh Britōt — a shiv'ata cycle for Musaf on the Shabbat of a bar mitsvah, by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:bibl.tei:title: שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה בְּרִיתוֹת
Shlōsh Esréh Britōt — a shiv'ata cycle for Musaf on the Shabbat of a bar mitsvah, by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer
tei:bibl.tei:author: Isaac Gantwerk Mayer
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: A shiv’ata is a sevenfold blessing inserted into the Musaf service on Shabbat. This shiv’ata was written for use at a bar mitsvah. Each stanza begins with an example of thirteen as used in our tradition, followed by an alphabetical acrostic. This piyyuṭ is for a bar mitsvah, where a boy turns thirteen. A companion piyyuṭ for a bat mitsvah, when a girl turns twelve, can be found here.

Note: “The CAUSE” is used to translate the Divine Name YHVH, based on the philosophical idea of God as the Prime Mover and on the interpretation of the Name as a causative form of the copula – “causes to be.” This translation also uses the plural pronouns They/Their/Them to refer to God as a pluralis majestatis, and to avoid the implications of God being assigned a gender. (Find Ibn Ezra’s commentary on Genesis 1:1 for a discussion of the pluralis majestatis when referring to God.) All divine referents (pronouns, epithets, names) are rendered in unicase.
